newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco quiet, Chicago winds down Nov barrels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco quiet, Chicago winds down Nov barrels.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline basis was steady on Monday as trade in November barrels wound down in Chicago, traders said.
Traders said high sulphur diesel differentials were also easing in Group Three on a large shipment into the Williams pipeline system due in the first December cycle.
Trade in the Chicago and Group Three cash markets was expected to remain light this week ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday weekend.
"It's very quiet," one trader said of discussion to open the week.

The Williams pipeline system, a key barometer of stocks in the Group Three market, opened the week with a relatively thin 18-day supply of gasoline and a relatively large 32-day supply of low sulphur diesel stocks on hand.

Chicago unleaded was talked 3.50/3.75 cents a gallon over the print for late-November deliveries, with first-cycle December barrels easing to 3.75/4.0 cents a gallon over NYMEX January unleaded futures.
Group Three unleaded was steady at 4.75/5.0 cents a gallon over NYMEX December unleaded for prompt deliveries and 3.75/4.0 cents over the print for later deliveries.
Group Three high sulphur diesel was talked 2.50/3.50 cents a gallon under the print, easing on a December 9 delivery into the regional pipes.
Low sulphur diesel differentials were steady in both markets, traders said.
